newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE MONEY MARKET LIQUID, RATES MIXED.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE MONEY MARKET LIQUID, RATES MIXED.

text.p: Short-term trading rates on Zimbabwe's money market were quoted mixed on Tuesday, dealers said.

They said the market closed with a Z$35 million surplus on Monday from Z$90.2 million previous, but added that the Reserve Bank had deemed the level of liquidity on Tuesday too low to warrant a treasury bill auction.

Meanwhile, discount houses were selling 91-day treasury bills in the secondary market at 17.50 percent, slightly down from the previous day's 17.55 percent while call money shed half a percentage point to 17.50 percent.
NCD bills maturing after 30, 60 and 90-days were quoted firmer at 19 percent from 18.50 (buying) but were being sold easier at 18 percent compared to 18.25 percent.
Bankers acceptance bills were quoted at 18.25 and 17.50 percent (buying and selling respectively), little changed from 18.25 and 18 percent.
